planted_defect: revocation of a delegated permission is never reflected in delegation_delegation_snapshot, so a revoked delegation keeps authorizing requests until the snapshot TTL expires

findings.trigger: revoke_delegation is called for a group whose members hold entries in delegation_snapshot
findings.consequence: revoked administrators retain effective delegated permissions until the snapshot is refreshed; the revocation contract is violated
findings.evidence: flawed-design.md: effective_permissions consults delegation_snapshot and falls back to a graph walk only when the snapshot is absent; revoke_delegation is not specified to invalidate the snapshot
findings.smallest_correction: specify that revoke_delegation invalidates every snapshot entry whose grant chain includes the revoked delegation, and make the graph walk the source of truth

findings.trigger: grant_delegation adds an edge below an already-cached subject
findings.consequence: effective_permissions can report a stale set for cached subjects, omitting newly granted permissions until TTL expiry
findings.evidence: flawed-design.md: delegation_snapshot is populated at grant time and no invalidation is specified for grants affecting descendant cache entries
findings.smallest_correction: specify a snapshot epoch bumped on every graph mutation, compared by effective_permissions before serving cache contents
